messages:
maria: Heads up — we're seeing JSON.parse errors in the Python SSE client when the server splits an event across TCP chunks. Happened in prod small canary, 2 failures so far.

chris: Which failure? partial token error or full garbled JSON?

maria: partial token. stack: JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 23 (char 22)

maria: raw (approx) from tcp dump — note chunk boundaries: 
```
chunk1: 'data: {"user":"alice","msg":"hi'
chunk2: ' there","id":42}

chunk3: 'data: {"user":"bob","msg":"ok","id":43}

'
```

raj: ah classic. the SSE spec uses "\n\n" as event delimiter, and each data line is prefixed with "data: ". If server splits inside a JSON string, clients that naively split on '\n\n' at decoder boundaries will run into partial events. You need to accumulate until you see a full blank-line delimiter.

chris: Exactly. Our JS client used TextDecoder + buffer.split('\n\n') which broke when the '\n\n' arrived split across two ArrayBuffer chunks.

sasha: @maria can you try the branch devex/sse-buffering? It switches to an event accumulator loop instead of instant split. Lightweight change.

maria: Pushed a quick repro and a small patch. Python reassembler i used: 
```py
buffer = ""
for chunk in resp.iter_content(chunk_size=None, decode_unicode=True):
    buffer += chunk
    while "\n\n" in buffer:
        event, buffer = buffer.split("\n\n", 1)
        data_lines = [l[6:] for l in event.splitlines() if l.startswith('data:')]
        payload = "\n".join(data_lines)
        try:
            obj = json.loads(payload)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            # partial JSON inside event (e.g. split inside string)
            # push event back and wait for more chunks
            buffer = event + "\n\n" + buffer
            break
        handle(obj)
```

chris: Nice. Two small notes: 1) avoid repeatedly concatenating large strings (use deque or list + join if using large throughput), 2) if server uses multiple 'data:' lines to intentionally include newlines, joining with '\n' is correct per spec.

raj: For node reader loop the pattern is similar. Use an inner while to drain all complete events and leave remainder in buffer. Pausing read is how you do backpressure: stop calling reader.read() and let the TCP window back up. That gives server natural slowdown.

maria: We're still seeing bursts where the client can't keep up => memory spikes. Any ergonomic backpressure strategy suggestions?

sasha: We should expose 'max_inflight_events' on the client side and have the runtime stop reading when count >= limit. When limit lowers, resume. Also add per-event small ack across control websocket so server can trim in-flight queue in Dedicated mode.

chris: For hosted API that's more work. Short-term: limit chunk_size and process events on a worker pool so the read loop doesn't block parsing. Also consider using sequence numbers in events so if reassembly fails we can request re-delivery or resume from seq.

raj: Another robust server-side fix: emit JSON as a single-line compact JSON in one 'data: ' line (escape internal newlines) or base64-encode payload into data: so client delimiters are clean. But that means extra encode/decode CPU.

maria: base64 would avoid delim issues but yeah overhead. For now i'll land the accumulator + max_inflight_events approach in the python client branch and run canary.

devops-bot: deploy-bot: rolled out canary deploy devex/sse-buffering to sse-canary-3 (region us-west2) at 2026-03-17T14:05:00Z :rocket:

maria: ok canary started. i'll watch memory and error rate for 30m and report. thanks folks :thumbsup:

sasha: if this still flakes tomorrow ping me and i'll add seq numbers and a small control socket for acks.

chris: opened a short doc in the repo: docs/streaming/client-guidelines.md with patterns and dos/don'ts. pls add anything you hit.

maria: will add repro steps and logs to that doc. good catch everyone.
